title: Shellfish and noodles with tomato-based sauce

content.title: About
content.content: The dish combines fresh shellfish (usually mussels), al dente noodles, and a tomato‑based sauce seasoned with garlic, basil, and olive oil. Shellfish provide high‑quality protein and minerals, while the noodles supply complex carbohydrates, and the tomato sauce adds vitamin C and lycopene.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Shellfish are one of the fastest‑growing seafoods; they can be fully cooked in 3–5 minutes.
Cooked tomatoes increase the bioavailability of lycopene, a powerful antioxidant.
The tradition of pairing seafood with pasta originated in Mediterranean cuisine, where sea flavors often meet tomato sauces.
Durum‑wheat noodles retain their shape in thick sauces, keeping the dish "al dente".
Shellfish are a rare non‑plant source of vitamin B12, essential for nerve health.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Shellfish contain high‑quality marine protein that supports muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Mineral source
items.content: Mussels are abundant in zinc, iron, and selenium, which aid immune function and antioxidant defense.

items.title: Lycopene in the sauce
items.content: Thermally processed tomatoes boost lycopene absorption, protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: When prepared with moderate olive oil, the dish remains low in saturated fats.

items.title: Cardiovascular support
items.content: Omega‑3 fatty acids in shellfish help lower triglycerides and improve vascular health.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to shellfish.

items.title: Contamination risk
items.content: Shellfish can accumulate toxins and heavy metals; purchase from reputable suppliers.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Tomato sauces often contain added salt; people with hypertension should monitor intake.

items.title: Digestive sensitivity
items.content: Large portions of shellfish may cause gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, tossing the noodles with the sauce and shellfish. Garnish with fresh basil, grated Parmesan, or a pinch of red pepper flakes for extra heat. A wide plate helps retain the aromatic sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh shellfish in a sealed container in the refrigerator for 1‑2 days. Cooked noodles and sauce can be stored separately in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat thoroughly to at least 75 °C before serving.
